svg.title: Roadster refill reports differ by configuration; a separate modeled example estimates gas flow
svg.desc: InsideEVs reports a two-to-six-hour refill and an under-30-minute goal for the 200-liter Thrust tank, which has about five seconds of boost. WIRED reports six to seven hours and a 30-minute reduction goal for the 600-liter Rocket system. A separate scenario assumes 80 kilonewtons for five seconds at 700 meters per second exhaust velocity, yielding about 114.3 kilograms per second and 571 kilograms total. The reports do not establish that these inputs describe the same configuration, and no tank mass is inferred.
svg.text: REFILL WINDOWS DEPEND ON WHICH ROADSTER.
Reported durations and targets are distinct from this article's conditional flow calculation.
External high-pressure nitrogen supply, per the report.
No fill pressure or tank mass is inferred for this system.
80 kN and about 5 s come from separate reports; combining them here is a scenario, not a measured run.
The calculation does not infer the gas mass in either tank or assign 80 kN to the 200 L or 600 L setup.
Tank inventory needs measured fill pressure, temperature, real-gas properties, usable residual pressure, and the thrust curve.
Sources: InsideEVs and WIRED, October 16, 2026. Refill values are reported; the flow example is modeled.
